AUTHOR: Kandimalla
TITLE: Automated Detection, Classification and Counting of Fish in Fish Passages With Deep Learning
REGION: Wells Dam fish ladder, Columbia River, Washington, USA (optical); Ocqueoc River, Michigan (sonar, out of scope)
SPECIES: Single 'fish' class for tracking; footage contains Chinook, Jack Chinook, Sockeye
DATA: Wells Dam Camera dataset (EyeSea, Xu and Matzner 2018), 24,000 frames at 30 fps, 13,405 with fish; Ocqueoc River DIDSON sonar dataset (not coded)
D_EV: Sec. 2.2.2.1: 'split the 24,000 frames ... into 19,200 images for training and 4800 images for testing by randomly selecting videos to have no overlap of videos'
R_EV: Sec. 2.2.2.1: 'We similarly downsampled and subsampled the test videos, resulting in three test sets' (all from the Wells Dam Camera dataset)
C_EV: Table 7 reports 'false positives (FP), false negatives (FN), ID switches (IDs), fragmentation (FM)' across initialization delays 6–17
E_EV: Sec. 4: 'We evaluated the performance of fish tracking (Table 7) including the overall duration of tracking, number of false positives and negatives, ID switches, fragmentation'
METR: MOTA, MT/PT/ML, FP, FN, ID switches, fragmentation
NOTE: Only the optical (Wells Dam fish ladder) component coded; DIDSON sonar detection/classification is out of scope (sonar-only). D4=Y: leakage concern explicitly addressed for sonar labeling ('reduce the potential that two nearly identical images will appear in both the training and test sets'); optical split is by video. C1 NR: confidence threshold mentioned only generically ('typically 0.5'), not stated for the models. C5 coded ID-switch handling because ID switches are measured and the initialization_delay parameter is tuned to suppress spurious tracks; no count-level verification. Paper says it counts fish but reports no counts or comparison with ladder counts, so E1=없음. PRE stated as ImageNet (text also says 80 classes). DSHR: public datasets analysed (EyeSea, FigShare), not new data.
